notes: Synthetic / anonymized judge training cases for PWF-20 (Diveye module 6). Evidence packs link existing FootageAsset ids — no real athlete names in case copy.

materials.title: White / yellow / red — decision tree
materials.body: White = valid performance. Yellow = penalty applied but dive stands (AIDA points / CMAS metres after penalty). Red = disqualification. Borderline calls usually sit on surface protocol, early/late start, or airway control in the first seconds after surfacing.

materials.title: AIDA surface protocol checklist
materials.body: After surfacing the athlete must complete the surface protocol within the allowed window: remove facial equipment, give the OK sign, and say “I’m OK” (or equivalent) without airway compromise. Incomplete or late protocol → yellow or red depending on severity and safety.

materials.title: CMAS start-window notes
materials.body: CMAS start timing is stricter than AIDA on early starts in several depth disciplines: an early start can be a full DQ (red) rather than a yellow with time penalty. Always apply the judging federation’s rulebook for the attempt.

trainingCases.title: Textbook white — DYN protocol
trainingCases.summary: Clear surface protocol; no safety concern.
trainingCases.scenario: Athlete surfaces on time, removes mask within the window, shows OK and speaks clearly. Markers show a clean protocol and a white-card stamp.
briefing: Watch surface → protocol → card markers in order.
Confirm airway stays open; no grab of the lane line.
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Protocol completed correctly with no penalty markers. Reference card is white.

trainingCases.title: Borderline yellow — lane contact
trainingCases.summary: Mid-dive penalty marker; dive otherwise completed.
trainingCases.scenario: A penalty marker fires before surface. Athlete finishes the protocol. Debate: incidental lane touch vs assisted propulsion.
briefing: Decide whether the contact warrants a yellow (penalty) or red (DQ for pull).
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Incidental contact with measurable effect → yellow with penalty, not a full pull DQ in this synthetic reference.
ruleHints: Yellow vs red on intentional pull

trainingCases.title: Hard red — BO watch
trainingCases.summary: Blackout watch after surface; safety overrides borderline protocol.
trainingCases.scenario: Protocol starts, then a BO-watch marker appears. Athlete loses airway control briefly; safety intervenes.
briefing: Prioritise safety signals over formal protocol timing.
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Loss of consciousness / airway after surface → red (DQ) with safety notes. Training focus: never “upgrade” to white after BO.

trainingCases.title: Borderline white — depth turn
trainingCases.summary: Bottom turn looks late but marker stays legal.
trainingCases.scenario: Bottom turn is visually late relative to the plate; surface protocol is clean. Reference panel kept white with a depth-marker note for training discussion.
briefing: Compare turn marker vs declared depth behaviour.
Surface protocol is secondary here — focus on turn legality.
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Synthetic reference: turn accepted; white card. Useful as a false-red trap for trainees.

trainingCases.title: Borderline yellow — delayed OK
trainingCases.summary: Surface OK delayed; no full BO.
trainingCases.scenario: Athlete surfaces, hesitates on the OK sign and speech. Airway remains open; no grab. Panel reference is yellow for incomplete protocol timing.
briefing: No dedicated card marker on this clip — judge from surface timing alone.
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Delayed / incomplete surface protocol without BO → yellow in this synthetic AIDA reference.
ruleHints: Yellow before red when airway OK

trainingCases.title: CMAS early start — red
trainingCases.summary: Federation-rule contrast: early start as DQ under CMAS.
trainingCases.scenario: CMAS embed-only clip with sparse markers. Scenario text states an early start relative to OT. Apply CMAS (not AIDA) start rules.
briefing: Judging federation is CMAS for this attempt.
Early start → red in this training reference (contrast with AIDA yellow/time penalty).
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Training contrast case: CMAS early start treated as DQ (red). Do not import AIDA yellow habits blindly.

trainingCases.title: HQ confirm — still white
trainingCases.summary: Same dive as case 01 at HQ quality; card should not flip.
trainingCases.scenario: HQ twin of the clean DYN. Trainees sometimes over-call after scrubbing; reference remains white.
briefing: Use HQ only to confirm protocol clarity.
Do not invent a yellow from compression artefacts.
trainingCases.referenceRationale: Same reference as the preview clean dive — white.

trainingCases.title: Hard red — assisted pull
trainingCases.summary: Clear intentional pull on the line after the penalty marker.
trainingCases.scenario: Same evidence pack as the borderline yellow, but the written scenario escalates: athlete clearly pulls for propulsion after the marker. Reference panel: red.
briefing: Re-read the scenario — same footage, different facts for this case.
trainingCases.referenceRationale: When the narrative establishes intentional pull, card upgrades from yellow training case to red.
